identity.name: Smurf Attack via ICMP Flooding
identity.summary: An attacker uses Windows command-line tools to send ICMP echo requests to a broadcast address, amplifying network traffic to overwhelm targets. Cortex detects this behavior as suspicious ICMP traffic
identity.description: An attacker uses Windows command-line tools to send ICMP echo requests to a broadcast address, amplifying network traffic to overwhelm targets. Cortex detects this behavior as suspicious ICMP traffic resembling a smurf attack.

expected_artifacts.description: ICMP traffic sent to broadcast IP

manual_steps: Not authored. Write and test cleanup before promotion.

biocs.name: Suspicious ICMP Traffic
biocs.description: Detection of ICMP echo requests sent to broadcast address with large payload size
biocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.NETWORK
| filter action_remote_ip = '192.0.2.1'
| filter dst_port = 1
| filter action_protocol = ENUM.ICMP
| filter action_bytes > 1000

abiocs.name: ICMP Broadcast Flooding
abiocs.description: Behavioral deviation detected when ICMP echo requests are sent to broadcast address with large payloads
abiocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.NETWORK
| filter action_remote_ip like '255.255.255.255'
| filter action_protocol = ENUM.ICMP
| filter action_bytes > 1000
| filter action_process_image_name = 'ping.exe'

xql_queries.name: Hunt for Smurf-like ICMP Traffic
xql_queries.query:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.NETWORK
| filter action_protocol = ENUM.ICMP
| filter action_remote_ip like '255.255.255.255'
| filter action_bytes > 1000
| comp count() by action_process_image_name
